domain: Climate Policy / Political Economy / Intergenerational Ethics
topic_summary: Analysis of three competing climate response frameworks—mitigation-priority, adaptation-priority, and degrowth—each reading the climate crisis kernel differently and emitting structurally distinct constraints with different victim sets, cost-bearer allocations, and intergenerational equity implications.

key_entities: Mitigation-Priority Coalition (IPCC, tech-optimist governments, renewable energy sector)
Adaptation-Priority Coalition (vulnerable nations, insurance sector, disaster management institutions)
Degrowth Movement (post-growth economists, climate justice activists, global South advocacy)
Future Generations (unborn/young populations bearing long-term climate costs)
Carbon-Intensive Industries (fossil fuel sector, heavy manufacturing)
Global Financial System (capital allocation mechanisms, discount rate authorities)
key_tensions: Present consumption vs future climate stability (mitigation vs all other approaches)
Global North emissions history vs Global South adaptation burden (justice vs efficiency)
Economic growth imperative vs planetary boundaries (degrowth vs both mainstream approaches)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Climate crisis as a coordination problem requiring collective action, where the shared commitment is 'preventing/managing climate harm' but readings disagree on what constitutes legitimate harm prevention and who bears costs
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Epistemic authority grounded in climate science consensus (IPCC) contested by political-economic interpretations of feasibility, justice, and growth compatibility
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: contested_stabilization (multiple authorities claim different readings of climate science implications)

readings.commitment: Legitimate climate response prioritizes emissions reduction to prevent future harm via technological transition within growth framework
readings.authority_grounding: IPCC carbon budget science + technological feasibility assessments + economic modeling assuming continued growth
readings.expected_structural_delta: Future generations primary beneficiaries; present generation (especially carbon-intensive sectors) bears transition costs; assumes growth-compatible decarbonization

readings.commitment: Legitimate climate response prioritizes near-term resilience building as mitigation politically/economically infeasible; accepts higher warming trajectory
readings.authority_grounding: Political realism about mitigation barriers + actuarial risk assessment + vulnerable nation survival imperatives
readings.expected_structural_delta: Present vulnerable populations primary beneficiaries; future generations and low-adaptation-capacity regions bear residual climate costs; front-loads expenditure

readings.commitment: Legitimate climate response requires planned economic contraction in Global North as mitigation within growth framework is physically/politically impossible
readings.authority_grounding: Planetary boundaries science + critique of green growth feasibility + climate justice/decolonial frameworks
readings.expected_structural_delta: Global South and future generations primary beneficiaries; Global North present consumption bears costs; rejects growth as constraint boundary

axiom_contradictions.basis: Mitigation-priority assumes decarbonization within continued economic growth is feasible; degrowth asserts this is thermodynamically/politically impossible. No framework can hold both 'growth-compatible transition is feasible' and 'growth must be abandoned' as simultaneously true.

Adaptation-priority treats mitigation as politically/economically non-viable and accepts higher warming; mitigation-priority treats sub-2°C warming as achievable necessity. A single framework cannot hold both 'mitigation is achievable' and 'mitigation has failed, accept warming' as foundational premises.

axes.human_readable: Mitigation-Priority Reading (Prevent Future Harm via Decarbonization)
axes.structural_delta: Emissions reduction prioritized to prevent >2°C warming; technological transition within growth paradigm; future-oriented cost-benefit analysis
axes.primary_observable: Carbon budget compliance trajectories; renewable energy deployment rates; climate finance allocation to mitigation vs adaptation
axes.selection_reason: Core reading with distinct intergenerational victim structure; highest training data availability requires critical generation

axes.human_readable: Adaptation-Priority Reading (Build Resilience, Accept Higher Warming)
axes.structural_delta: Near-term resilience investments prioritized over emissions cuts; accepts 2.5-4°C trajectory; vulnerability-focused resource allocation
axes.primary_observable: Adaptation finance flows; disaster preparedness infrastructure investment; insurance penetration in vulnerable regions
axes.selection_reason: Structurally distinct beneficiary set (present vs future); political realism grounding challenges mitigation reading

axes.human_readable: Degrowth Reading (Planned Contraction in Global North)
axes.structural_delta: Economic growth rejected as constraint boundary; planned consumption reduction in high-income nations; climate justice as decolonial project
axes.primary_observable: GDP trajectory advocacy; Global North consumption metrics; sufficiency-based policy proposals vs efficiency-based
axes.selection_reason: Axiom-contradictory to mitigation reading on growth feasibility; lowest training data representation requires dark matter probe

axes.human_readable: Carbon Removal Backstop (Negative Emissions Technology Dependence)
axes.structural_delta: All three readings implicitly or explicitly depend on future carbon dioxide removal availability; constraint on what overshoot is 'acceptable'
axes.primary_observable: CDR scaling assumptions in IPCC pathways; investment in DAC/BECCS; overshoot scenario prevalence
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: shared dependency across readings but not a distinct reading itself; omega material on technological lock-in

axes.structural_delta: Cost-benefit analysis discount rates determine present vs future cost allocation; readings differ on legitimate rates
axes.primary_observable: Discount rates in climate policy models; Stern vs Nordhaus debate framing in policy documents
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: methodological rope underlying victim structure but not independent reading; captured in intergenerational framing

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Shared dependence on future negative emissions technology across all readings
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Not a distinct reading but a shared technological dependency; omega material on lock-in risk if CDR fails to scale

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Intergenerational cost weighting mechanism underlying victim structure
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Methodological rope captured within each reading's intergenerational framing; low independent analytical yield

omegas.description: If carbon dioxide removal fails to scale, do all three readings collapse into adaptation-priority by default? The mitigation reading's carbon budget overshoot scenarios depend on CDR backstop.
omegas.source: Deferred axis carbon_removal_backstop + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Is absolute decoupling of emissions from GDP thermodynamically achievable at required scale and speed? If not, mitigation-priority reading collapses into degrowth reading, validating axiom contradiction.
omegas.source: Axiom contradiction between mitigation_priority and degrowth_reading + F34 epistemic boundary

omegas.description: At what warming threshold does adaptation become non-viable (e.g., wet-bulb temperature exceeding human survivability)? Adaptation-priority reading may front-load costs into an unlivable future.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium: survival as background assumption) + adaptation_priority victim structure

omegas.description: Adaptation-priority grounds authority in 'mitigation is politically infeasible,' but this feasibility claim may be self-fulfilling. Does treating mitigation as infeasible make it so?
omegas.source: Authority grounding critique of adaptation_priority reading

omegas.description: All three readings risk treating Global South as object rather than agent. Degrowth reading centers justice but may impose Northern framework; mitigation/adaptation assume Northern policy authority.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan: who controls framing) + extraction_summary tensions
